After Qe5+, White simply plays Rxe5! winning the queen. The forcing_lines output said Qe5+ Rxe5 with -9 for Black, which means +9 for White.

So **Rge4** is the winning move! It defends the e1 rook and creates multiple threats (the queen will be trapped). Black's best try Qf4+ loses the queen to Rxf4+. Any other queen move also loses material.

**Best move:** Rge4

**Main line:** Rge4 Qf4+ Rxf4+ Kxe1 Rxh4

**Motif:** The move defends a loose piece (the e1 rook) while simultaneously attacking the h4 pawn and trapping Black's queen, which loses material on any move.

**Coaching note:** When your piece is attacked, before moving it to safety, look for where you can move it that accomplishes TWO things: defends the attacked piece AND creates a new threat or pins/traps an opponent piece. Here, moving the rook to e4 defends e1, attacks h4, and traps the queen—Black loses no matter what. When you feel under pressure, multi-purpose moves often turn defense into advantage.
